title: Reshaping High Energy Physics Applications for Near-Interactive Execution Using TaskVine
problem: Late-stage HEP analysis applications require frequent iterative refinement and re-execution across thousands of nodes, with long iteration cycles impeding scientific discovery. Scaling these applications while maintaining interactivity demands comprehensive changes to storage, data management, task scheduling, and application design.
motivation: Reducing iteration times in large-scale HEP analysis workflows accelerates the pace of scientific discovery.
method: The paper applies TaskVine, a task scheduling system, alongside open-source frameworks Coffea and Dask to reshape late-stage HEP analysis applications. It implements systemic changes across the full stack including storage system redesign, data management strategies, task scheduling optimization via TaskVine, and application architecture modifications to enable near-interactive execution at scale.
key_novelty: Demonstrating that TaskVine-based task scheduling combined with systemic stack redesign enables near-interactive HEP analysis execution across thousands of nodes while maintaining data reduction workflows.
contributions: Demonstration of reshaping late-stage HEP analysis for near-interactive execution at petabyte scale
Comprehensive stack redesign across storage, data management, scheduling, and application layers
Performance evaluation on opportunistic campus clusters with effective scaling to 7200 cores
Integration of TaskVine, Dask, and Coffea frameworks for large-scale iterative analysis

metrics.other: effective scaling to 7200 cores on opportunistic campus clusters

primary_theme: Interactive petabyte-scale HEP analysis via task scheduling
